named_confounds: genre composition shift (domestic_realist dominant early, juvenile dominant late)
small early-period sample (752 of 6766 works before 1876)
date_confidence heterogeneity (effect is -0.013 in low-confidence works)
author productivity higher among late works
rationale: Every work has one passage (n_passages=1), so the rate is a 0/1 flag for DISTANCE_TRAVEL. I split works into early (<1876) and late (>=1876). For each genre I took the mean over works of late minus early, then averaged the 8 genres with equal weight. Effect = +0.018, with a 95% CI from a 400-replicate bootstrap stratified by genre x period of [-0.007, 0.042], which includes zero. Composition checks: the genre mix changes a lot across the cutoff (domestic_realist is 37% of early works vs 15% of late; juvenile is 11% vs 35%). Because juvenile has a high travel rate and domestic_realist a low one, the raw decade means rise from about 0.05 to 0.12. Most of that rise is a composition effect. Within genres the changes are mixed: juvenile, other and sensation go up, while adventure, collection and domestic_realist go slightly down. Origin, date_confidence and n_editions are roughly balanced across periods. Author productivity is a bit higher late. Restricting to high-confidence dates gives +0.031 with CI [-0.006, 0.064], still including zero. Low-confidence dates give -0.013. A WLS model adjusting for genre, origin, date_confidence, log editions and log author productivity, with author-clustered SEs, gives +0.012 with CI [-0.011, 0.034]. No specification excludes zero. The early cells are small (47-280 works per genre), so a modest true increase cannot be ruled out. The passage IDs only show that the construct appears in the texts; they do not show a trend.
